page: Amazon Web Services r5.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server instance powered by Intel Xeon 8175M processors. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this configuration delivers 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system features 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It includes a 25 Gbps baseline network interface but does not feature local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core and memory performance. The r5.metal achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng tests, Passmark CPU scores, and memory bandwidth, with uncached read speeds reaching 222.69 GB/sec. Database operations are highly efficient, as demonstrated by strong Passmark database scores and Redis SET performance of 74.16 million operations per second. However, single-core performance remains average, and LLM text generation speeds are weak to poor, reflecting the lack of specialized hardware accelerators or newer instruction sets like AMX.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal architecture eliminates virtualization overhead, maximizing the utility of the massive 768 GB memory pool. This makes it a highly resource-dense option for large-scale, memory-intensive workloads. The server is suited for high-performance databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, large-scale software compilation, and enterprise applications requiring direct hardware access.
